candidates.exact_span: a. The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory toxicity-testing obligation; whether this section applies to a given facility/outfall determines if WET monitoring was required for FY2025.

Scopes toxicity requirements to final outfall 001; different readings of which discharge points qualify as covered outfalls change limit applicability, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence evaluation for other points.

Sets the dilution benchmark against which chronic lethal and sub-lethal effects are judged; a different critical-dilution value would change whether reported WET results are treated as exceeding the applicable toxicity threshold.

Defines the dilution concentrations used to determine NOEC and test failure; different interpretation of the required series affects how a reported toxicity result maps to pass/fail at or below the critical dilution.

candidates.exact_span:
TEST SPECIES AND METHODS           Ceriodaphnia dubia / Method 1002.0 (EPA-
                                    821-R-02-013 or latest version)
                                    Pimephales promelas/ Method 1000.0
                                    (EPA/821/R-02-013 or latest version)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies which species and EPA methods must be used; whether alternate species, methods, or 'latest version' readings apply changes which monitoring counts as required and which reported results are valid for toxicity compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers sample-type requirements to PART I; without resolving that cross-reference, whether grab/composite or other sample conditions were required—and whether absent results reflect non-required monitoring or missing required evidence—remains uncertain.

candidates.exact_span:
The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest
      effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control
      (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the operative compliance metric for lethal toxicity; different readings of NOEC calculation or the 95% confidence criterion change whether a given test result is classified as within or exceeding the toxicity limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic lethal test failure is
      defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a
      test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when a WET test constitutes a lethal limit exceedance; interpretation of 'statistically significant' or 'at or below the critical dilution' changes compliance determinations for reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span:
Chronic sub-lethal test failure is defined as a
      demonstration of a statistically significant sub-lethal effect (i.e., growth or reproduction)
      at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a separate sub-lethal exceedance standard; whether growth or reproduction effects count as failures at or below critical dilution affects toxicity compliance outcomes distinct from lethal failure.

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the
      procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this
      permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a repeat-testing obligation when acceptability criteria are not met; whether a deficient test triggers a repeat requirement changes if monitoring was satisfied and whether the available evidence is adequate or represents missing required data.

Imposes a minimum sample count for toxicity testing; fewer than three samples may mean the monitoring obligation was not fulfilled and that reported or absent results should be treated as inadequate evidence rather than ordinary compliance data.

candidates.exact_span:
Test Acceptability Criteria        ≥80% survival of all control
                                    organisms.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a control-survival threshold for valid tests; if control survival is interpreted as failing this criterion, the repeat requirement applies and the original result may not support a compliance comparison or may indicate missing adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Holding time *                     36 hours for first use
candidates.computation_change_reason: Limits how long samples may be held before testing; samples tested beyond this window may be deemed invalid, changing whether absent or reported results constitute adequate evidence of required monitoring.
